newsitem.title: IRAN: Iranian editor to face trial in open court.
newsitem.headline: Iranian editor to face trial in open court.

text.p: An Iranian newspaper editor detained since April on espionage charges will be tried in an open court, the secretary-general of the Islamic Human Rights Commission (IHRC) said in remarks published on Wednesday.
Faraj Sarkuhi, editor of the monthly Adineh (Friday), was arrested in April for trying to leave the country illegally.
The case has attracted international attention with intervention by the U.S. group Human Rights Watch, French-based Reporters Sans Frontieres (Reporters Without Borders), and the German government.
In a letter smuggled out of Iran, Sarkuhi alleged that he was held for six weeks and tortured by the Iranian secret service in Tehran late last year to force him to confess to spying for Germany.
IHRC secretary-general Mohammad Hassan Ziaifar was quoted by Iran News daily as saying in Tehran that Sarkuhi and his family had been in contact with the organisation.
He said the journalist had sent a letter to the IHRC on July 8 in which he confessed to certain violations of the law and strongly rejected the interference of foreign governments.
"Sarkuhi has openly named Germany, asking also for some other foreign countries not to get involved in this domestic issue," Ziaifar said.
The official said Sarkuhi had openly admitted having had contact with some foreign embassies in Tehran although he said there was no ill-will behind his contacts.
Sarkuhi's wife, Farideh Zebarjad, lives in Germany and has expressed concern that he was being held as a bargaining chip to put pressure on Germany.

Relations between Tehran and European Union countries are strained over a German court ruling in April that Iran's leadership ordered the killing of a group of Kurdish exiles in Berlin in 1992. Iran denies the charges.

Human Rights Watch said in an open letter to the head of Iran's judiciary, Ayatollah Mohammad Yazdi, last month it feared the charges might have been brought to punish Sarkuhi for his activities as a writer and to intimidate other independent-minded writers in Iran.
